newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares drop on expectations of slow rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares drop on expectations of slow rate cut.

text.p: Greek equities fell another 1.33 percent on Thursday on low volume said market watchers said the drop was due to expectations of interest rates declining at a slower pace in the future.

"The general share index dropped on Thursday because of market expectations of milder interest rate cuts. Wednesday's bond auction signalled that rates might have bottomed out for now," said analyst Nikos Kostopoulos at Commercial Securities.
But other brokers said they did not think the bonds' auction had an adverse effect on the bourse today.

"I do not think that the bourse's drop was a result of the auction. It is, rather, the outcome of a general bad sentiment in the market and the index's attempt to stabilise before rising to new highs," said broker Alexandros Devletoglou, of Devletoglou Securities.
The market is moving downwards and will pierce the previous support level of 1,250 points in the short term, Kostopoulos added.
"The new support level is set between 1,150 and 1,200 points. On March 4, it had made an intra-day low of 1,159 points, which is a sign of its downside risk," he said.
European bourses slipped sharply early on Thursday, weighed down by another fall on Wall Street and concerns about interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic.
It has never been proved that a fall in Wall Street could trigger a drop in the Athens bourse.
"Statistical studies conducted over and over again have not shown any correlation between the two bourses," said Kostopoulos.

The Athens general share index ended 1.33 percent or 17.11 points lower at 1,268.67 points from Wednesday's 1,285.78 after opening at 1283.25. Turnover was 8.1 billion drachmas on volume of 2.6 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 168 to 44 with 25 issues unchanged on 237 traded.
Construction closed 2.71 percent lower and banks lost 1.58 percent. Industrials settled 0.97 percent lower and small caps dropped 0.90 percent. Investment shares ended 1.29 percent lower.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 986.00-1024.00. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, lost 75 drachmas to settle at 5,750.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $39.77-$41.46. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 1,484-1,658 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
